steps.title: Collect field mosquitoes
steps.instruction: Capture 200–300 adult female An. darlingi or An. deaneorum using BG‑malaria traps or human‑attraction technique (protected) between 18:00 and 21:00 in a peridomicile malaria‑endemic area.

steps.title: Transport in field cages
steps.instruction: Place captured mosquitoes (30–50 per cage) into 750 mL spherical plastic cups (field cages) covered with mesh, add a moistened cotton ball soaked in 10 % sucrose, cover with damp towels and a black 50 L plastic garbage bag, and store the cages in a 50 L foam box for transport to the laboratory.

steps.title: Fast before blood feeding
steps.instruction: On the day after collection, remove the 10 % sucrose solution from the cages 6 h before the planned blood meal to induce fasting.

steps.title: Blood feed on chicken
steps.instruction: Restrain a live adult chicken (2–3 kg) on top of each cage and allow mosquitoes to feed for 15 min; optimal feeding time is 17:00–18:00 (GMT‑4).

steps.title: Anesthetize and identify species
steps.instruction: Four days after blood feeding, place the cups in a 5 L foam box with ice for 15 min, then identify each mosquito under a stereomicroscope using the dichotomous keys of Consoli & Lourenço‑de‑Oliveira.

steps.title: Induce oviposition (wing removal)
steps.instruction: For each identified An. darlingi or An. deaneorum, remove one wing with dissection tweezers, place the wing‑less mosquito in a 90 mm Petri dish lined with moistened 80 g filter paper (90 mm), five mosquitoes per dish, and store dishes in a 10 L foam box under insectary conditions.

steps.title: Daily transfer to fresh dishes
steps.instruction: Each day, move live mosquitoes to new Petri dishes with fresh moistened filter paper, discard dead individuals, and re‑moisten the paper using a 3 mL plastic Pasteur pipette; repeat for three consecutive days before egg washing.

steps.title: Wash eggs with hypochlorite
steps.instruction: Connect a 0.22 µm vacuum filtration system to a vacuum pump; using a 500 mL squirt bottle filled with distilled water, transfer all eggs from the filter paper onto the filter, perform an initial water rinse, then add 1 L of 0.25 % sodium hypochlorite (prepared from 10 % stock) and filter after 30 s; repeat this hypochlorite‑water cycle three times, alternating with 1 L distilled water washes.

steps.title: Transfer eggs to rearing pans
steps.instruction: Place washed eggs onto rearing pans (30.3 × 22.1 × 7.5 cm) whose walls are lined with filter paper and fill each pan with 1 L distilled water, ensuring the eggs cover the walls; after each day, squirt water onto the walls with a wash bottle to stimulate hatching.

steps.title: Start larval feeding schedule
steps.instruction: From day 1 post‑egg transfer, feed larvae according to Table 1: Instar 1 – ground food sieved through 63 µm once daily with a brush; Instar 2 – ground food sieved through 125 µm twice daily with a brush; Instar 3 – ground food sieved through 250 µm three daily with a spatula; Instar 4 – same 250 µm food three times daily with a spatula.

steps.title: Add yeast and perform water changes
steps.instruction: On day 3 after egg transfer, add 5 mL of 1 % yeast solution to each pan using a 5 mL beaker; on day 5 change water by transferring larvae to a clean pan (200 larvae per pan) and thereafter change water every Monday, Wednesday and Friday, separating larvae by instar with 63, 125 or 250 µm sieves; add 5 mL of 1 % yeast solution at the end of each water‑change day.

steps.title: Collect pupae for emergence
steps.instruction: From ~10 days after egg washing, collect pupae daily with a 3 mL plastic Pasteur pipette and transfer them to 500 mL spherical plastic pupae containers placed inside a screened 30 × 30 cm cage containing a cotton pad soaked in 15 % honey solution; each container holds 300–500 pupae.

steps.title: Maintain adults on honey solution
steps.instruction: Keep emerged adults at 26 ± 1 °C, 70 ± 10 % RH, 12 h light/12 h dark, providing ad libitum 15 % honey solution on a cotton pad; replace the pad every Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.

steps.title: Induce mating by light stimulation
steps.instruction: When 1 500–2 000 three‑ to five‑day‑old mosquitoes are available, transfer 800–2 000 (≈1:1 male:female) into a screened 61 × 61 × 61 cm cage; six hours before induction remove honey and set temperature to 24 ± 1 °C with a night photoperiod; at 18:00 expose the cage to a white LED beam (5 mm, 6 000 K, 18 000 MCD, 2 Hz pulse) positioned 61 cm above the cage for four cycles of 10 min on/10 min off; repeat the light cycles for 5–7 consecutive evenings.

steps.title: Feed females on chicken during induction
steps.instruction: After the final light cycle, allow females to feed on restrained chicken for 15 min during the first 4–6 days of induction, then restore normal insectary conditions (26 ± 1 °C, 70 ± 10 % RH, 12 h light/12 h dark).

steps.title: Natural mating and oviposition (later generations)
steps.instruction: From the F5–F6 generation onward, allow natural copulation by keeping 3–5‑day‑old mosquitoes under standard conditions for three days, then blood‑feed on chicken for 15 min on day 4; place four oviposition containers (walls lined with filter paper, ~200 mL distilled water) inside the cage 48 h after blood feeding; from the F8 generation use smaller cages (46 × 46 cm then 30 × 30 cm).

steps.title: Routine egg collection and handling
steps.instruction: Three days after blood feeding, remove oviposition containers, discard dead mosquitoes, pour all water into a transition pan lined with filter paper, wait 1 min for eggs to adhere, then use one filter paper to seed two rearing pans for first‑instar larvae; label pans with generation and transfer date; squirt water onto pan walls to stimulate hatching; clean and discard oviposition‑container water as described in the cleanliness section.

steps.title: Routine larvae rearing
steps.instruction: Rear ~600 first‑instar larvae per pan in 1 L distilled water; on day 2 add 5 mL of 1 % yeast solution; on day 4 transfer larvae to fresh pans (no filter paper) at 300 larvae per pan; thereafter follow the water‑change schedule (Monday: first‑ and second‑instar pans; Friday: all pans except newly seeded egg pans) adding 5 mL of 1 % yeast solution at each change; maintain water temperature at 24 ± 1 °C; keep larval density at ≈250 per pan for later instars; expect pupation after 9–15 days.

steps.title: Pupae management
steps.instruction: Collect pupae daily with a Pasteur pipette, place 300–500 pupae into a 500 mL pupae container inside a 30 × 30 cm cage with a cotton pad soaked in 15 % honey; record pupae production and mortality on the cage badge; do not mix pupae older than 5 days in the same cage.

steps.title: Adult maintenance and blood feeding
steps.instruction: Provide adults with 15 % honey solution ad libitum, replacing the cotton pad Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday; on Wednesdays remove honey at 08:00, and at 17:30 (GMT‑4) offer a blood meal: prepare 500 mL glass bottles of bovine blood collected in 30 U.I./mL swine sodium heparin (add 600 µL anticoagulant per 100 mL blood) and store at 4 °C ≤7 days; invert four 180 mL Styrofoam cups, add 3 mL blood to each, cover with a PTFE membrane piece, warm cups with water to maintain blood at ~37 °C, allow mosquitoes to feed for 30 min; after feeding replace the honey‑soaked cotton pad and discard used cups according to the cleanliness section; record feeding date on the cage badge and feeding form.

steps.title: Prepare infection reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the following solutions as described in the Recipes section: 10 % sucrose (5 g sucrose + water to 50 mL, store ≤7 days at 4 °C, equilibrate 1 h at RT before use); 0.25 % sodium hypochlorite (75 mL 10 % bleach + 2 925 mL ddH₂O, total 3 L, store ≤7 days at RT); 0.5 % sodium hypochlorite (50 mL 10 % bleach + 950 mL ddH₂O, total 1 L, store ≤7 days at RT); 15 % honey (150 mL honey + 850 mL ddH₂O, total 1 L, store ≤7 days at 4 °C, equilibrate 1 h at RT); 1 % yeast (10 g yeast extract + 990 mL ddH₂O, total 1 L, store ≤7 days at 4 °C, equilibrate 1 h at RT); 70 % ethanol (700 mL absolute ethanol + 300 mL water, total 1 L, store at RT); 2 % mercurochrome stock (0.2 g mercurochrome + 9.8 g water, total 10 mL, store at RT); 0.2 % mercurochrome working (1 mL 2 % stock + 9 mL water, total 10 mL, store at RT); 6 % lab detergent (60 mL 100 % detergent + 940 mL water, total 1 L, store at RT); 0.02 % peracetic acid (700 µL 15 % peracetic acid + 499.3 mL water, total 500 mL, store at RT).

steps.title: Collect P. vivax infected blood
steps.instruction: After informed consent, draw venous blood from symptomatic patients into heparinized tubes; keep the tubes at 37 °C throughout handling using a water bath or thermos bottle.

steps.title: Process infected blood
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the blood at 500 × g for 5 min at 37 °C; carefully remove plasma and white blood cells and replace them with heat‑inactivated human AB⁺ serum (56 °C, 30 min) at a 1:1 ratio with the patient’s blood.

steps.title: Load blood into membrane feeder
steps.instruction: Pipette 1 000 µL of the prepared blood‑serum mixture (or whole blood) onto a Parafilm membrane (20 cm × 20 cm) covering the reservoir of a feeding cup (650 mL cup for feeding, 2 000 mL cup for infected blood), then connect to the Hemotek feeding station.

steps.title: Prepare mosquitoes for infection
steps.instruction: Select 60–100 female mosquitoes aged 3–5 days, fast them for ≥12 h, and place them inside a 650 mL blood‑feeding cup (field cage) for the DMFA.

steps.title: Feed mosquitoes on infected blood
steps.instruction: Allow the females to feed for 30 min; after feeding, place the feeding cup in a 5 L foam box with ice for 1–2 min to anesthetize the mosquitoes.

steps.title: Separate fed and unfed mosquitoes
steps.instruction: Remove the mesh netting, visually sort engorged females (distended dark abdomen) from unfed ones; euthanize unfed mosquitoes by immersing them in a 100 mL beaker containing 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Maintain infected mosquitoes
steps.instruction: Transfer engorged females to an infection cage, re‑attach the mesh netting, and keep them under the standard insectary conditions (26 ± 1 °C, 70 ± 10 % RH, 12 h light/12 h dark) with 15 % honey solution until dissection.

steps.title: Dissect midguts for oocysts (day 7)
steps.instruction: At 7 days post‑infection, anesthetize mosquitoes on ice for 1–2 min, transfer them to a 100 mL beaker with 70 % ethanol, then move each to a Petri dish containing 1× PBS; place 5–10 drops of 5 µL PBS on a glass slide, pick a mosquito with fine forceps, and transfer it to a PBS drop; dissect the midgut using two 0.20 mm needles (one to stabilize thorax, one to pull abdomen), remove Malpighian tubes, then transfer the midgut to a new slide with 3 µL 0.2 % mercurochrome, cover with a coverslip, wait 2 min, and count oocysts at 10–20× magnification.

steps.title: Dissect salivary glands for sporozoites (day 14)
steps.instruction: Repeat steps E1–E3; using two 0.20 mm needles, secure the head and thorax, pull the head rightward to expose the glands, sever them from the head, and collect the glands into a 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube containing 15 µL ice‑cold RPMI‑1640; process 2–10 pairs per tube, centrifuge 20 s, crush with a matching pestle 30 strokes, re‑centrifuge 20 s, then load 10 µL onto a Neubauer chamber, wait 10 min, and count sporozoites in 25 squares; calculate sporozoites per mosquito as (count/25) × 10 000 / (number of mosquitoes in pool).

steps.title: Clean rearing pans and containers
steps.instruction: Wash rearing pans, pupae containers, and oviposition containers with a soft sponge and 6 % lab detergent, rinse with running water, then spray the interior with 0.02 % peracetic acid solution and allow to air‑dry at room temperature.

steps.title: Maintain distilled water container
steps.instruction: Refill the distilled‑water container daily; clean it weekly using the same 6 % detergent rinse and 0.02 % peracetic acid spray as for other containers.

steps.title: Dispose of water and waste
steps.instruction: Before discarding water from pans, verify no larvae remain; if L1/L2 larvae are present, add boiling water, wait 2 min, then discard; discard water down the sink.

steps.title: Clean cages after use
steps.instruction: Euthanize remaining mosquitoes, spray cage interior with 70 % ethanol, remove and discard paper containing dead insects as bio‑hazard waste, wipe walls and bottom with 70 % ethanol and a paper towel, then line the bottom with fresh paper.

steps.title: Decontaminate blood‑feeding materials
steps.instruction: For items containing ≤2 mL blood (e.g., glass feeders, Hemotek discs, tubes), soak in 1 % bleach solution for ≥30 min, then rinse and dry; for larger blood‑containing tubes (>2 mL), place in a covered container for autoclaving; wash feeders with neutral detergent and a brush, rinse, dry, and store; dispose of sharps in a sharps container and all biological waste in appropriate bins.
